claim: The UK IPO's 'Music creators' earnings in the digital era' report published an official errata correcting its Chapter 6 per-million-stream figures after discovering the original calculation omitted a 5% PRS/ICE administration fee.
stance_target: Reliability of published creator-income figures and the need to trace corrections before citing
scope_conditions: UK, music streaming creators (songwriters and featured performers), 2020 streaming-rate figures underlying the errata; published by the Intellectual Property Office (IPO), a UK government body
quoted_support: This calculation failed to take into account PRS/ICE administration fees, which would reduce revenues by 5%. Reduced by this amount, the true figure for a month (=four weeks) should therefore be £1,176... the annual figure if the same level of streams were sustained across a year would be £15,288.
region: UK; Western-only, not generalizable to Southeast Asia

claim: The report's errata also corrected a typing error in the featured-performer per-million-stream figure from GBP 1,210 to GBP 1,201, changing the annualised estimate from GBP 15,730 to GBP 15,613.
stance_target: Reliability of published creator-income figures and the need to trace corrections before citing
scope_conditions: UK, featured performers on music streams, 2020 basis
quoted_support: due to a typing error, our estimated figure for what a typical featured performer would earn from a million 2020 streams was stated as £1,210... The true estimated figure should be £1,201... and the annual estimated figure for a typical featured performer would be £15,613.

claim: Both errata-corrected annual estimates (GBP 15,288 for songwriters, GBP 15,613 for featured performers) sit below commonly cited living-wage benchmarks, meaning even the IPO's own recalculated per-million-stream earnings do not by themselves constitute a full living income for a typical creator earning from streams alone.
stance_target: Income from content/music creation frequently falls short of a living wage even for creators who reach meaningful scale (1 million streams/month)
scope_conditions: UK, music streaming creators only, assumes 1 million streams sustained every month for a year (an atypical, high-scale assumption)
quoted_support: the annual figure if the same level of streams were sustained across a year would be £15,288.

claim: The UK IPO published the raw survey microdata and survey instrument underlying the 224-page report, making the dataset re-analysable by third parties, which is unusual in creator-income research.
stance_target: Data availability and reproducibility in creator-income research
scope_conditions: UK Creators' Earnings Survey; published alongside the main report on GOV.UK
quoted_support: UK creators' earnings survey raw data, MS Excel Spreadsheet, 357 KB... UK creators' earnings survey tables, MS Excel Spreadsheet, 1.34 MB.

claim: Any citation of the IPO report's Chapter 6 per-million-stream earnings figures that uses the original (pre-errata) numbers (GBP 1,238/GBP 1,210) is citing a known-incorrect figure.
stance_target: Methodological correctness in citing this report
scope_conditions: UK IPO report, Chapter 6, 2020-basis streaming earnings estimates
quoted_support: In addition, due to a typing error, our estimated figure for what a typical featured performer would earn from a million 2020 streams was stated as £1,210...
